overview: This one-page Department of State list of papers indexes correspondence and reports concerning Taiwan’s economic affairs between 1930 and 1939. Its principal entries concern Vice Consul Charles S. Reed II’s report on Taiwan’s policy of fostering domestic industries, the report’s confidential circulation among several U.S. departments and the Governor-General of the Philippines, a related report titled “Taiwan and the South Seas,” and Emmerson’s later report on an investigation of Taiwan by Japanese bankers.

people.name: Charles S. Reed II
people.role: U.S. Vice Consul at Taihoku; author of a report on Taiwan’s economic conditions

people.name: John K. Emmerson
people.role: Author or reporting officer associated with the 1939 Taihoku report

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers on Taiwan economic matters
subfiles.about: An index records reports and related correspondence on Taiwan’s industrial policy, regional economic relations, and an investigation by Japanese bankers.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists papers numbered 7–11, beginning with a July 19, 1930 report from Vice Consul Reed at Taihoku on Taiwan’s adoption of Japan’s policy of fostering domestic industries and manufactures. Follow-up entries from January and February 1931 document its confidential distribution to the War, Navy, and Commerce Departments and to the Governor-General of the Philippines, as well as Commerce Department interest in “Taiwan and the South Seas.” The final entry records a December 4, 1939 report by Emmerson concerning an investigation of Taiwan by Japanese bankers and notes cross-references to other decimal-file headings.

interest: The sheet is useful as a concise map of material that may have circulated beyond the surviving bundle, revealing both the subjects studied by U.S. officials and the departments that received the resulting intelligence. It connects Taiwan’s state-supported industrialization with American strategic interest in the Philippines and the South Seas, while the 1939 entry points to concern about Japanese banking activity on the island. Its administrative annotations, including confidentiality instructions, an evaluation of Reed’s report as “EXCELLENT,” and cross-references to other decimal-file categories, also illuminate State Department recordkeeping and information-sharing practices.
